cells.tense: You're in it now, and the steadiness is yours to spend.
cells.verb: gathering what you've been through into one direction and holding it
cells.place: where things get weighed and set right
cells.ask: offer the steadiness outward once, this week — bring what you're holding into a room that isn't yours, and let the shared joy that comes back tell you what it was for.
cells.core: You've gathered yourself and you're holding the line — not clenched, just clear. Something was worth protecting, you protected it, and the same steadiness that got you here is now free for something that has nothing to defend.
cells.sheetLine: You've gathered yourself and you're holding the line.

cells.tense: You're already braced for what's next, and next hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: defending a direction nobody has actually challenged yet
cells.ask: rest the mind that keeps re-scoring the fight — sit with what's actually in front of you, let one thing stay unresolved, and let your next move come from what you feel rather than from what you're guarding against.
cells.core: You're holding the line against an attack that's still in your head. Every version of what's coming gets countered before it arrives — double-checked, second-guessed, moved a beat early to be safe. The bracing is doing to you what nothing outside has managed to do.
cells.sheetLine: You're fighting a battle that hasn't started yet.

cells.tense: The moment passed and you're still standing where it left you.
cells.verb: holding ground you already gave away
cells.ask: let one ending be an ending — keep the part of what you built that still holds, let the person you were choose one of two ways and close the other, and trust that driving from feeling is safe once there's a form around it.
cells.core: You gave up the defense without knowing it. Somewhere back there you decided something was worth standing for, and then you didn't stand — and you've been standing at that spot ever since, holding the ghost of it. The turning at the center isn't there anymore. That's what's out of balance.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped defending something without noticing you had.

cells.tense: The pen's in your hand, but you're calling it the room's writing.
cells.verb: steadily steering, and calling it just how things are
cells.ask: do one piece of it out where someone can see — take what you've been quietly holding together and build it somewhere it can be looked at, and let the insight that surfaces show you whose hand steadied it.
cells.core: You're the one holding this steady. What looks like the situation holding itself together is you gathering the parts, choosing when to press and when to wait, keeping things fair without announcing it. The steadiness is running; the credit hasn't been claimed.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding it steady and calling it just how things are.
